svg.title: The interpolation step preceding this argument supplies those certificates at the real nodes. Explicitly, at k + 1 distinct nodes ti, let li be the Lagrange basis and Bk = P Pk r=0 |[tr]li|. A i degree-k family with nodal derivative allowance Abq has (ASP1) allowance BkRkAbq: expand li(Rz) and bound Rr ≤Rk. For optional exponential vertices the nodal hypothesis is on ef(ti) −1. When its allowance is at most 1/2, log(1 + y) has bounded derivatives on [−1/2, 1/2] and | log(1 + y)| ≤ 2|y|. The finite chain rule therefore bounds the nodal logarithm through the same spatial order. Interpolate this logarithm, and only then exponentiate by (ASP1). The condition BjR2(3q) ≤1, with its fixed derivative constants included in Bj, pays this last exponential step. This explains why the source can use polynomial dependence of the log without asserting polynomial dependence of the exponential.
